title: Explore the customer table
prompt: List customer names and countries, ordered alphabetically by customer name.
starter: SELECT \nFROM customers;
answer: SELECT customername, country FROM customers ORDER BY customername;
hint: Choose customername and country from customers, then ORDER BY customername.

title: Countries represented
prompt: Return each distinct country represented in customers, sorted alphabetically.
starter: SELECT DISTINCT \nFROM customers;
answer: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers ORDER BY country;
hint: DISTINCT removes repeated rows in the output.

title: Orders in 2024
prompt: List ordernumber and orderdate for orders placed during calendar year 2024, oldest first.
starter: SELECT ordernumber, orderdate\nFROM orders\nWHERE
answer: SELECT ordernumber, orderdate FROM orders WHERE orderdate >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND orderdate < DATE '2025-01-01' ORDER BY orderdate;
hint: Use two date boundaries; the end boundary is exclusive.

title: Orders with customer names
prompt: List every ordernumber and its customername, sorted by ordernumber.
starter: SELECT \nFROM orders o\nJOIN customers c USING (customernumber)
answer: SELECT o.ordernumber, c.customername FROM orders o JOIN customers c USING (customernumber) ORDER BY o.ordernumber;
hint: An order joins to exactly one customer using customernumber.

title: Products that never sold
prompt: List productcode and productname for products with no order details, sorted by productname.
starter: SELECT p.productcode, p.productname\nFROM products p
answer: SELECT p.productcode, p.productname FROM products p LEFT JOIN orderdetails od USING(productcode) WHERE od.ordernumber IS NULL ORDER BY p.productname;
hint: A LEFT JOIN preserves products that have no matching orderdetails; select the missing side with IS NULL.

title: Customers per country
prompt: List country and number of customers as customer_count, sorted by country.
starter: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count\nFROM customers
answer: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY country;
hint: Each country needs its own group.

title: Count all customers' orders
prompt: List customernumber and count of orders as order_count for EVERY customer (including those with zero orders), sorted by customernumber.
starter: SELECT c.customernumber, \nFROM customers c
answer: SELECT c.customernumber, COUNT(o.ordernumber) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o USING(customernumber) GROUP BY c.customernumber ORDER BY c.customernumber;
hint: Start at customers, LEFT JOIN orders, and COUNT(o.ordernumber) instead of COUNT(*).

title: Avoid multiplying payment totals
prompt: Homework 8, Query 3: list customernumber, customername, and SUM of payments as total_payments for customers with payments. List each once, sorted by customername. Do not join orders: it multiplies payments and drops customers with no orders.
starter:
SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername, SUM(p.amount) AS total_payments
FROM customers c
JOIN payments p USING (customernumber)
JOIN orders o USING (customernumber)
GROUP BY c.customernumber, c.customername
ORDER BY c.customername;
answer: SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername, SUM(p.amount) AS total_payments FROM customers c JOIN payments p USING(customernumber) GROUP BY c.customernumber,c.customername ORDER BY c.customername;
hint: An unnecessary join to orders multiplies payment rows. SUM(DISTINCT amount) is not safe when two payments have equal amounts.

title: Orders with subtotal above 1,000
prompt: List ordernumber and SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) as subtotal for orders whose subtotal exceeds 1000. Sort by ordernumber.
starter: SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal\nFROM orderdetails
answer: SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal FROM orderdetails GROUP BY ordernumber HAVING SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) > 1000 ORDER BY ordernumber;
hint: The condition is on an aggregate, so it belongs in HAVING.

title: Exclude every oversized purchase
prompt: Homework 8, Query 5: list productcode and productname of products that NEVER appear in an order detail with quantityordered > 48. Include products never ordered. Sort by productname.
starter:
SELECT DISTINCT p.productcode, p.productname
FROM products p
INNER JOIN orderdetails od USING(productcode)
WHERE od.quantityordered <= 48
ORDER BY p.productname;
answer: SELECT p.productcode, p.productname FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orderdetails od WHERE od.productcode = p.productcode AND od.quantityordered > 48) ORDER BY p.productname;
hint: Find bad productcodes (quantity > 48), then exclude them. Never-ordered products must remain.

title: All orders tied for biggest subtotal
prompt: Homework 8, Query 4: list ordernumber and subtotal for every order tied at the maximum subtotal, sorted by ordernumber. The subtotal is SUM(quantityordered * priceeach).
starter: SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal\nFROM orderdetails\nGROUP BY ordernumber
answer: WITH totals AS (SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal FROM orderdetails GROUP BY ordernumber) SELECT ordernumber, subtotal FROM totals WHERE subtotal = (SELECT MAX(subtotal) FROM totals) ORDER BY ordernumber;
hint: Aggregate orderdetails first in a CTE. Compare each subtotal to MAX(subtotal) of that CTE.

title: One order, not one line item
prompt: Homework 8, Query 2: list each ordernumber ONCE if it has at least one orderdetail with quantityordered > 50. Sort by ordernumber. Fix the provided query.
starter:
SELECT o.ordernumber
FROM orders o
JOIN orderdetails od USING(ordernumber)
WHERE od.quantityordered > 50
ORDER BY o.ordernumber;
answer: SELECT DISTINCT o.ordernumber FROM orders o JOIN orderdetails od USING(ordernumber) WHERE od.quantityordered > 50 ORDER BY o.ordernumber;
hint: A joined row is an order line, not an entire order. More than one line can satisfy the filter.

title: Payment duplication trap
prompt: Repair the query so that customers with payments appear once with the correct sum, even if they have multiple orders or no orders.
starter:
SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername, SUM(p.amount) AS total_payments
FROM customers c
JOIN payments p USING(customernumber)
JOIN orders o USING(customernumber)
GROUP BY c.customernumber,c.customername
ORDER BY c.customername;
answer: SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername, SUM(p.amount) AS total_payments FROM customers c JOIN payments p USING(customernumber) GROUP BY c.customernumber,c.customername ORDER BY c.customername;
hint: The orders join contributes nothing to the requested total and multiplies payment rows.

title: Keep every tied maximum
prompt: Fix Homework 8 Query 4. Return ordernumber and subtotal for every greatest-subtotal order, ordered by ordernumber. Avoid a tie-breaker that makes tied values appear different.
starter:
SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal
FROM orderdetails
GROUP BY ordernumber
ORDER BY subtotal DESC, ordernumber
FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY;
answer: WITH totals AS (SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal FROM orderdetails GROUP BY ordernumber) SELECT ordernumber, subtotal FROM totals WHERE subtotal=(SELECT MAX(subtotal) FROM totals) ORDER BY ordernumber;
hint: Ties apply to every ORDER BY expression; a unique ordernumber breaks ties. Compare to MAX(subtotal) instead.

title: Exclude the most common customer country
prompt: Homework 8, Query 1: count orders by year as order_year and num_orders, excluding countries with the most CUSTOMERS (including those with zero orders and all ties). Sort by year.
starter:
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.orderdate) AS order_year, COUNT(*) AS num_orders
FROM orders o JOIN customers c USING(customernumber)
WHERE c.country NOT IN (
 SELECT country FROM customers JOIN orders USING(customernumber)
 GROUP BY country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS WITH TIES
)
GROUP BY order_year ORDER BY order_year;
answer: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.orderdate) AS order_year, COUNT(*) AS num_orders FROM orders o JOIN customers c USING(customernumber) WHERE c.country NOT IN (SELECT country FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS WITH TIES) GROUP BY order_year ORDER BY order_year;
hint: The innermost query must count customers in customers, not joined orders. JOIN orders changes who is counted.

title: Calculated sales value
prompt: List productcode, productname, and the expression msrp - buyprice as margin for every product, ordered by productcode.
answer: SELECT productcode, productname, msrp - buyprice AS margin FROM products ORDER BY productcode;
hint: You can calculate a new SELECT expression and assign it an alias with AS.
source: Adapted from lecture: Basic SELECT Queries

title: Filter with AND
prompt: Find customername and creditlimit for USA customers whose creditlimit is less than 50000, ordered by customername.
starter:
SELECT customername, creditlimit
FROM customers
WHERE
answer: SELECT customername, creditlimit FROM customers WHERE country = 'USA' AND creditlimit < 50000 ORDER BY customername;
hint: Two predicates are required; combine them with AND.
source: Adapted from lecture: Basic SELECT Queries

title: Preview an UPDATE safely
prompt: Before changing customer credit limits, SELECT customernumber, customername, creditlimit for customers whose creditlimit is less than 50000. Sort by customernumber. This is a read-only preview; updates belong in the Playground.
starter:
-- Preview the rows your UPDATE would affect
SELECT 
FROM customers
WHERE
answer: SELECT customernumber, customername, creditlimit FROM customers WHERE creditlimit < 50000 ORDER BY customernumber;
hint: Use SELECT with the same WHERE you would later use in UPDATE.

title: Preview a DELETE safely
prompt: Before deleting old orders, show ordernumber and orderdate of all orders before 2024-01-01, sorted by orderdate then ordernumber. Do not actually delete records.
starter:
SELECT ordernumber, orderdate
FROM orders
WHERE
answer: SELECT ordernumber, orderdate FROM orders WHERE orderdate < DATE '2024-01-01' ORDER BY orderdate, ordernumber;
hint: A SELECT preview reduces the risk of deleting rows you meant to keep.

title: Join using ON
prompt: Return ordernumber and customername for every order, ordered by ordernumber. Use explicit JOIN ... ON to connect orders to customers.
starter:
SELECT o.ordernumber, c.customername
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON
answer: SELECT o.ordernumber, c.customername FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customernumber = c.customernumber ORDER BY o.ordernumber;
hint: Both tables contain customernumber; qualify each side when using ON.
source: Adapted from lecture: Inner join variations

title: Find unmatched customers
prompt: List customername of every customer who has placed NO orders, sorted by customername. Customers with no orders must be included.
starter:
SELECT c.customername
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o USING(customernumber)
WHERE
answer: SELECT c.customername FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o USING(customernumber) WHERE o.ordernumber IS NULL ORDER BY c.customername;
hint: The orders primary key becomes NULL for customers without a match.
source: Adapted from lecture: OUTER JOIN uses

title: Count orders, not motorcycle lines
prompt: The lecture warns that COUNT(*) after joining orders → orderdetails → products counts line items, not qualifying orders. Return a single column motorcycle_orders: how many distinct orders include a motorcycle product?
starter:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS motorcycle_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN orderdetails od USING(ordernumber)
JOIN products p USING(productcode)
WHERE p.productline = 'Motorcycles';
answer: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT od.ordernumber) AS motorcycle_orders FROM orders o JOIN orderdetails od USING(ordernumber) JOIN products p USING(productcode) WHERE p.productline = 'Motorcycles';
hint: The sample dataset has an order containing TWO motorcycle products. COUNT(DISTINCT od.ordernumber) fixes the row meaning.

title: Sum all items in qualifying orders
prompt: For every order that contains at least one Motorcycle product, list ordernumber and the total quantity of ALL products in the order as total_ordered. Sort by ordernumber. Avoid filtering out non-motorcycle line items before SUM.
starter:
SELECT od.ordernumber, SUM(od.quantityordered) AS total_ordered
FROM orderdetails od JOIN products p USING(productcode)
WHERE p.productline = 'Motorcycles'
GROUP BY od.ordernumber
ORDER BY od.ordernumber;
answer: SELECT od.ordernumber, SUM(od.quantityordered) AS total_ordered FROM orderdetails od WHERE od.ordernumber IN (SELECT od2.ordernumber FROM orderdetails od2 JOIN products p USING(productcode) WHERE p.productline = 'Motorcycles') GROUP BY od.ordernumber ORDER BY od.ordernumber;
hint: Use one subquery to select qualifying ordernumbers, then sum all orderdetails for those orders.

title: Customers holding the largest payment
prompt: Find customernumber and customername of ALL distinct customers whose payment amount equals the maximum payment amount, including ties. Sort by customernumber.
starter:
SELECT DISTINCT c.customernumber, c.customername
FROM customers c JOIN payments p USING(customernumber)
WHERE p.amount =
answer: SELECT DISTINCT c.customernumber, c.customername FROM customers c JOIN payments p USING(customernumber) WHERE p.amount = (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM payments) ORDER BY c.customernumber;
hint: MAX(amount) returns one scalar. More than one payment can equal that value, so keep all matching customers.
source: Adapted from lecture: Legal scalar subqueries

title: Orders from top-paying customers
prompt: List ordernumber, orderdate, customernumber for orders placed by ANY customer who made a payment with the largest single payment amount. Include all tied customers. Sort by ordernumber.
starter:
SELECT ordernumber, orderdate, customernumber
FROM orders
WHERE customernumber IN (
answer: SELECT ordernumber, orderdate, customernumber FROM orders WHERE customernumber IN (SELECT customernumber FROM payments WHERE amount = (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM payments)) ORDER BY ordernumber;
hint: MAX gives a scalar; customers matching the maximum form a vector. Use IN rather than =.
source: Adapted from lecture: Scalar super challenge

title: Vector IN: shared states
prompt: List customernumber and customername for customers in states containing at least two customers. Exclude customers without a known state. Sort by customernumber.
starter:
SELECT customernumber, customername
FROM customers
WHERE state IN (
answer: SELECT customernumber, customername FROM customers WHERE state IN (SELECT state FROM customers WHERE state IS NOT NULL GROUP BY state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2) ORDER BY customernumber;
hint: The inner query returns a vector of state codes. Filter grouped states with HAVING.

title: Never ordered in 2024
prompt: List customernumber and customername of every customer who placed NO orders in 2024, including customers with no orders at all. Sort by customernumber. A 2023 order does not prove there is no 2024 order.
starter:
SELECT DISTINCT c.customernumber, c.customername
FROM customers c JOIN orders o USING(customernumber)
WHERE o.orderdate < DATE '2024-01-01'
ORDER BY c.customernumber;
answer: SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customernumber=c.customernumber AND o.orderdate >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND o.orderdate < DATE '2025-01-01') ORDER BY c.customernumber;
hint: Exclude the set of customers who DID order during 2024. NOT EXISTS also keeps customers without any orders.
source: Adapted from lecture: Vector-valued subqueries (2015 example)

title: Customers ordering each year
prompt: Using a table subquery orders_with_year with ordernumber, customernumber, order_year, list each year and COUNT of distinct customers as num_customers. Sort by year.
starter:
SELECT order_year, COUNT(*) AS num_customers
FROM (
 SELECT ordernumber, customernumber, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM orderdate) AS order_year
 FROM orders
) AS orders_with_year
GROUP BY order_year
ORDER BY order_year;
answer: SELECT order_year, COUNT(DISTINCT customernumber) AS num_customers FROM (SELECT ordernumber, customernumber, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM orderdate) AS order_year FROM orders) AS orders_with_year GROUP BY order_year ORDER BY order_year;
hint: The inner rows represent orders. COUNT(*) counts orders, even when the same customer made more than one.

title: Average order subtotal
prompt: Return one column avg_order_subtotal: the average of per-order subtotals (for orders having at least one detail), NOT the average of individual detail costs.
answer: SELECT AVG(subtotal) AS avg_order_subtotal FROM (SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal FROM orderdetails GROUP BY ordernumber) AS per_order;
hint: First make one row per order in a FROM subquery, then average its subtotal column.

title: Markup through a derived table
prompt: List productname, buyprice, msrp and percentage markup as markup for products with a markup of at least 90%, using a subquery in FROM named product_markups. Sort by productname.
starter:
SELECT productname, buyprice, msrp, markup
FROM (
 SELECT productname, buyprice, msrp,
        (msrp - buyprice) / buyprice * 100 AS markup
 FROM products
) AS product_markups
WHERE
answer: SELECT productname, buyprice, msrp, markup FROM (SELECT productname, buyprice, msrp, (msrp - buyprice) / buyprice * 100 AS markup FROM products) AS product_markups WHERE markup >= 90 ORDER BY productname;
hint: The outer WHERE can use markup because the inner SELECT has already created the alias.
